metadata.name: Romanization of Marathi -- UNGEGN 4.0
metadata.description:
The United Nations recommended system was approved in 1972 (II/11) and amended in 1977
    (III/12), based on a report prepared by D. N. Sharma. The tables and their corrections were
    published in volume II of the conference reports

    There is no evidence of the use of the system either in India or in international cartographic
    products.

    Marathi (Marāṭhī) uses the alphasyllabic script Devanāgarī.
notes:
Additional characters (absent in Hindi):
       ळ ḷa
       ऍ ă (abbreviated: कॅ kă)
Ligatures may be formed with r as the first component: 'ऱ्य': 'rya' 'ऱ्ह': 'rha'
Typical are ligatures ending in h: न्ह nh, म्ह mh, ल्ह lh, व्ह vh.
The following independent characters are sometimes used: अि i, अी ī, अु u, अू ū, अे e, अै ai.

Diffed against the UN Romanization of Marathi for Geographical Names table as
 published in the WGRS Report on the Current Status of UN Romanization Systems
 for Geographical Names, version 4.0 (March 2016) (eki.ee/wgrs/rom1_mr.htm;
 also unstats wgrr4marathi), which gives the Hindi table plus the Marathi
 additions: ळ ḷa, ऍ ă (abbreviated कॅ kă), the ऱ्य/ऱ्ह and -h ligatures, and the
 independent अि i … series.

Fixed against the source: the abbreviated ऍ form कॅ (U+0945) was not encoded
 and is now rendered ă; the corrupt 'note[3]' rule (from some + 0939) was
 removed. The ॲ ê and ऑ ô rows have no row in the source table and are kept as
 practical extensions; the ऱ row likewise extends the source's ligature-only
 use of ऱ.
